title: Card Spec
description: Schema for evidence-card specifications authored by humans and stored as YAML under target-contracts/cards/. Validates the *authoring surface* of a card (the slots a card author fills in); the runtime emission surface (validation_state, provenance) is validated by card_output.schema.json. See plan section 'Evidence Card Framework' (A2) and the compose-dashboard behavioral spec (B1) for the runtime semantics of the fields below.

card_id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier for this card across versions. Same card_id + same version + same resolved inputs + same release_pin must produce byte-identical deterministic-field output (card-invariance discipline, A2).

version.description: Semantic version of this card spec. Bumps with method/threshold changes. Pre-release suffixes (-rc, -beta) allowed.

question.description: One-sentence statement of what this card answers. May contain {} template-string interpolations resolved at compose time (e.g., {target.symbol}, {indication.label}). Note: these are NOT CEL predicates; they are template-string substitutions performed during card rendering.

applies_when.description: List of CEL-compatible simple-predicate-subset strings. ALL predicates must evaluate to true (logical AND) for the card to be in scope. Cards that fail applies_when are excluded from the dashboard at compose time, NOT run-and-flagged. Evaluator grammar specified in B1 'compose-dashboard behavioral spec' subsection (2). Context-object schema specified in subsection (3).

derived_from.description: OPTIONAL. Declares this card as a DERIVED card whose method reads upstream cards' outputs (instead of, or in addition to, raw data products). Each entry names an upstream card_id. A cross-reference validator (validators/validate_cards.py::validate_derived_from_refs) uses this list to verify every referenced card_id resolves to a live card (or to a historical alias `from`->`to` in vocabularies/card_id_aliases.yaml). NOTE: the stronger 'emits the fields this card reads' field-level reachability check is NOT yet implemented — this list is verified for card EXISTENCE only.

consumed_by.description: OPTIONAL. The card→skill binding, MANY-TO-MANY with per-host role (plan Part 5 / card-binding SoT). One entry per skill that hosts this card; a multi-homed card carries N entries with per-host role. Cross-checks (in validators/validate_cards.py): (a) `lens` names a question `short` or conditioner id in vocabularies/target_profiling_axes.yaml (or the `self_contained` sentinel for inline-verdict skills); (b) role/verdict_source consistency vs the resolver; (c) reconciliation against the skills-side CARDS/SUB_SKILL_CARDS literals (validate-only). The verdict-bearing edge set stays DERIVED from rule_id→resolver→gate; this block records + reconciles it, it does not author it.

lens.description: The ontology axis this host reads the card under: a question `short` or conditioner id from target_profiling_axes.yaml, OR the `self_contained` sentinel when the host resolves its verdict inline (no gate short).

role.description: The card's role in this host. verdict=feeds a verdict; corroboration=confidence; stratification=patient-selection; display=verdict-inert render facet.

verdict_source.description: How the host resolves its verdict: resolver (declarative resolvers/<gate>.resolver.yaml), inline (in the skill's run.py), or none (display/descriptive). role:verdict requires resolver|inline.

compose_into_profile.description: OPTIONAL (default true). false = standalone-only; the card is NOT composed into target-profile under this host's lens.

compose_reason.description: OPTIONAL. Why this (often foreign-composition) edge exists, e.g. which resolver rung needs the card's rule in this host's fired-set.

order_hint.description: OPTIONAL. Advisory ordinal within the host's card list. NOT the byte-order authority — the committed literal governs order (validate-only phase).

axis_edge.description: OPTIONAL. Marks this card as a CROSS-AXIS EDGE — evidence that joins two biological axes (rather than a single-axis measurement). Formalizes what was previously only header prose (plan Part 5 / Part 6). `reports_into` (a question short in target_profiling_axes.yaml) is cross-checked in validators/validate_cards.py.

anchor.description: The outcome/anchor axis of the edge (a measurement_type or question short), e.g. crispr_lof_dependency, clinical_outcome_os.

partner.description: The conditioning/stratifying axis, e.g. mutation_status, paralog_family, genomic_alteration_status.

required_inputs.description: Catalog refs the card consumes. Each entry resolves at compose time against the active data_mode (latest_approved | pinned | exploratory). May be empty ONLY for COMPOSED cards (cards that declare `derived_from:` upstream card_ids); leaf cards must declare at least one product_id. Composed-card empty-array eligibility is checked by the cross-reference validator, not the JSON Schema.

product_id.description: Product identifier the card consumes. Resolves against EITHER a data-catalog manifest id (the primary namespace; e.g. depmap-gygi-protein-abundance-per-protein-v1) OR a registered product_id in target-contracts/vocabularies/products.yaml. validate_cards.py checks this referentially against the sibling data-catalog + products.yaml (WARNING on an unresolved id; graceful-skip when data-catalog is absent).

indication.description: OncoTree code or {indication} template placeholder resolved from the dashboard context.

release_pin.description: Specific manifest_id (for pinned mode) or {release_pin} template placeholder.

subgroup_catalog.description: Subgroup-catalog manifest_id, for cards that stratify by molecular subgroup.

optional.description: When true, this input is non-blocking — the card runs even if the product is unavailable, and emits 'data_unavailable' labels for fields derived from it. Useful for companion datasets (e.g. RNAi as a companion to CRISPR). Default: false (input is required).

methods.description: Method CLIs the card invokes. Methods are deterministic. Cards do not call models or web APIs directly.

call.description: Method CLI name (matches a method module in the methods repo, e.g., 'dge-deseq2', 'depmap-chronos'). Resolved to an in-process import of methods.<module> by compose-dashboard's live-reader layer.

module.description: OPTIONAL (T11, 2026-08-11): the importable methods-repo module path backing this call, e.g. 'gnomad_constraint' or 'driver_role_overlay.cli'. When present WITH `entrypoint`, compose-dashboard's generic dispatcher can invoke the reader directly without a hand-written _dispatch_* function — collapsing the ~30 pure-passthrough dispatchers into data. Defaults to `call` with hyphens→underscores when omitted.

entrypoint.description: OPTIONAL (T11, 2026-08-11): the module-level function the generic dispatcher calls, e.g. 'read_target_summary' or 'build_summary'. Called as fn(target=target, indication=indication) (+ data_context/subgroup_context when the fn's signature declares them). Only consulted for cards WITHOUT a bespoke _dispatch_* entry in CARD_DISPATCHERS; bespoke dispatchers (multi-method merges, positional-arg readers) are unaffected.

args.description: Keyword arguments passed to the method CLI. Values may contain {target}, {indication}, {release_pin}, {subgroup_spec} template placeholders.

outputs.description: Declarative description of what the card emits. The shape here defines what populates summary.json + figure.svg + plot_data.parquet for this card.

summary_fields.description: Names of fields that must be present in the card's emitted summary.json. Used by compose-dashboard's post-invocation validation (B1 § compose-dashboard subsection 5) to gate the validation_state. Each entry may be a bare string (biology-agnostic field, emitted unconditionally) OR an object with `name` + optional `lens_conditional_on` marker (field emitted only when a specific optional lens is invoked — e.g. `adc_grade` gated on `modality` lens). Bare-string form is preserved for backward compatibility; the reviewer-driven arch upgrade A2 (2026-07-08) adds the object form to prevent lens-only fields from leaking into biology-first invocations.

name.description: Field name (same shape as bare-string form).

lens_conditional_on.description: When set, this field is emitted only when the named optional lens is invoked at runtime. The rules engine treats the field as absent when the lens is not invoked; downstream consumers (target-profile LLM synthesis, provenance.yaml) must handle absence gracefully. Enables clean separation between biology-first outputs (always emitted) and lens-conditional outputs (e.g., ADC/TCE letter grades gated on the modality lens).

description.description: Optional per-field description surfaced in the card manifest.

summary_fields_vocabulary.description: Optional: for categorical summary_fields, declare the exhaustive set of values the method may emit. Consumed by validators/validate_interpretation_rules.py to confirm rule (card_id, field, value) triples are reachable. Map of field_name (must appear in summary_fields) -> list of allowed string values. Cards may omit this during the pure-data transition; validator emits a warning rather than an error.

summary_fields_record_schemas.description: Phase 4 (2026-07-15) — Declare record shapes for list-typed summary_fields (e.g. per_subgroup_metrics: [{stratum, class, subgroup_n, ...}]). Rules matching these fields use `when.in_record` (interpretation_rules.schema.json). Map of field_name → object describing the record's key names + expected value types. Per key, value spec is either `enum: [...]` (categorical), a JSON-schema type string ('integer', 'boolean', 'string'), or an object with an `enum` key. See target-contracts/docs/design/IDAS_SUBTYPE_PIPELINE.md for the list-typed card convention.

oneOf.comment: Nested list-of-records: a summary_field record may carry a key whose value is itself a list of records (one level of nesting, e.g. per_subgroup_metrics[].proxy_normal_windows[]). record_schema maps each nested leaf key to a flat type/enum spec.

figure.description: Iter-1b single-figure declaration. Identifier for the canonical figure type emitted by this card. Backward-compatible with cards that emit one figure; for multi-figure cards (iter-2+), use the `figures` array instead.

figures.description: Iter-2 multi-figure declaration. Cards may emit multiple figures with different visual representations of the same underlying analysis (e.g., waterfall + histogram for a distribution). The renderer reads `preferred_surfaces` to pick which figure to embed per output surface. The method CLI emits ALL listed figures to staging; the framework's renderer chooses per-context.

id.description: Stable identifier for this figure variant (e.g., 'waterfall', 'histogram_kde').

preferred_surfaces.description: Which renderer surfaces should prefer this figure variant. Renderers iterate their surface and pick the first matching figure.

primary.description: If true, this is the default figure when no preferred_surfaces match. Exactly one figure per card should be primary.

plot_data.description: Identifier for the canonical plot_data.parquet schema this card emits (e.g., 'long_format_paired_samples'). Parquet schemas live in target-contracts/schemas/plot_data/.

interpretation_hints.description: Rules that map output metrics to a categorical interpretation_call. Evaluated in order; first matching rule wins. Predicates use the same CEL-compatible subset as applies_when (B1 § compose-dashboard subsection 2).

if.description: CEL-compatible predicate evaluated against the card's emitted summary fields (NOT against the dashboard context — interpretation predicates are scoped to summary fields only).

call.description: The interpretation label emitted when the predicate evaluates true (e.g., 'strong upregulation', 'not informative').

dominant.description: EG4 (iter-2): if true, this interpretation_call is treated as a DOMINANT signal in fit_level scoring. The synthesis layer's dominant-signal-plus-confirmation rule rates the modality 'strong' when ANY primary card emits a dominant call AND no primary card emits a non-informative call. Card-authors opt in per-call to mark which of their calls represent discovery-driving signal (e.g., 'lineage-restricted: single tissue', 'structurally druggable: covalent pocket', 'actionable alteration'). Cards without any dominant calls fall back to ratio-based scoring (current iter-1b behavior). Backward-compatible: absent or false → no behavior change.

thresholds.description: Named thresholds referenced by applies_when and interpretation_hints predicates (e.g., THRESHOLD.expression_p95_min). Extracted to a separate block per T1.5 — magic numbers in predicates are the failure mode this pattern guards against. Threshold names are referenced in predicates as THRESHOLD.<name>; the validate_cards.py validator checks referential integrity.

threshold_roles.description: OPTIONAL (2026-09-12). Declares, per threshold name, that the cutoff is applied SOMEWHERE OTHER THAN a card predicate, so THRESHOLD_UNUSED must not ask for it to be deleted. The `thresholds:` block holds two different kinds of number: cutoffs a predicate compares against, and parameters an upstream method or reader already applied before the card sees a field (a stratification alpha, an effect-size floor, a model hyperparameter). Only the first kind can ever be predicate-referenced, so the unused-threshold warning fired permanently for the second and told authors to remove numbers the method needs. A role entry is a CHECKED claim, not a suppression: `method_parameter` must name one of THIS card's own methods[].call, and any threshold a predicate DOES reference may not be declared here at all (MISDECLARED_THRESHOLD_ROLE), which is what makes the declaration go stale loudly if the card later starts interpreting the value itself.

role.description: method_parameter: the named method applied this cutoff upstream; the card documents it for reviewability. reader_gate: the skill-side reader applies it while shaping the card's fields, so it cannot be anchored to a method call and needs a prose note instead.

consumed_by.description: REQUIRED when role is method_parameter: the methods[].call entry on this card that applies the cutoff. Checked against this card's own methods: block, the same way a resolver's driving_rule is checked against its own rung.

note.description: REQUIRED when role is reader_gate (nothing machine-checkable anchors that case, so the prose IS the review surface). Optional for method_parameter, where `consumed_by` is verified.

caveats.description: Known limitations of the question or methods. Surfaced in the rendered card panel and in the evidence_package's per-card block.

warning_predicates.description: Optional. Named warning predicates that fire (or don't fire) against the emitted output. When a predicate fires, the card's validation_state becomes 'passed_with_warnings' and the warning_id is surfaced in the dashboard. Predicates use the same CEL-compatible subset; evaluated against the card's emitted summary fields.

message.description: Human-readable message surfaced in the dashboard when this warning fires.

tier.description: Phase 4 (2026-07-15) — Optional annotation of which channel-precedence tier this card's evidence belongs to. Used by validators to enforce tier-appropriate applies_when predicates (target-tier cards should not reference indication.* or subtype.* keys). Enum: target | indication | panel | subtype. Cards without tier tag are un-classified (backward-compat for pre-Phase-4 cards).

interpretation.description: Authored interpretation INTENT (2026-09-11). REQUIRED exactly when no interpretation rule keys on this card (no `when.card_id` match in any interpretation-rules/*.rules.yaml), FORBIDDEN when rules exist — the rules are ground truth, so declaring intent alongside them can only contradict them. Before this field the rule-less cards were one undifferentiated bucket and the health feed could not report interpretation debt because it could not see it. `rules_pending` = the card's categorical class is a substantive claim about the TARGET (expression, selectivity, dependency, safety, tractability, translational readiness) that an axis should consume; tracked debt, and the published debt count. `informational` = the class describes the EVIDENCE BASE (annotation completeness, assay/literature coverage) or the INDICATION COHORT rather than the target; per target_profiling_axes.yaml conditioner axes 'refine the questions but are not themselves questions', so no target verdict may key on them. `descriptive` = the card emits no categorical class at all (no outputs.summary_fields_vocabulary), so there is nothing for a rule's `equals:`/`in:` to match. ENFORCEMENT: validate_cards.py _interpretation_declaration_check.

status.description: Card build/wiring state (2026-08-12). `wired` (the default when OMITTED) = has a live method + dispatcher + landed product. `placeholder_not_wired` = declared in the contract but no method/product yet (compose-dashboard surfaces it in excluded_at_compose, exclusion_source=data_blocked_at_compose; SK#373). `dormant_pending_data` = a method exists but the card is gated off because its data source has not landed (applies_when-excluded at runtime). `superseded` (added 2026-08-19) = the card's capability is provided elsewhere (e.g. wired at the method level in another skill), so the card is retired-as-duplicate but NOT hard-deleted (card_id is a data contract); it must be consumed by no skill/dashboard and carries a `superseded_by` note in caveats. ENFORCEMENT (validate_cards.py): a card whose status is NOT `wired` MUST NOT appear in any dashboard_spec `required_cards` — it belongs in `placeholder_cards`. This keeps `required_cards` meaning 'must produce' rather than 'may be silently not_wired'.

subgroup_stratification.description: Subgroup-panorama layer (2026-07-16) — Optional attestation block declaring whether this card enumerates a target's evidence across molecular subgroups (the DESCRIPTIVE subgroup panorama). Consumed by validators/validate_cards.py grain-check: a card with status:live MUST bind a per-sample stratified reader (read_stratified_* / build_*_panorama) — NOT an aggregate-substrate method whose values are baked at emit time. `tier: target` cards may NOT carry this block (scope-invariant target evidence never stratifies). Cards without the block are non-stratified (backward-compat).

eligible.description: True when the card's biology genuinely varies by subgroup (author attestation, PR-reviewed — filter 1 of the two-filter card-selection rule).

status.description: live = bound to a per-sample stratified reader, panorama emits per_subgroup_metrics. blocked_needs_per_sample_reader = biology varies but the bound method returns an emit-time aggregate (filter 2 fails); the card is honestly tagged as not-yet-stratifiable and the grain-check forbids it from declaring per_subgroup_metrics. out_of_scope = deliberately not stratified this iteration.

axes.description: Subgroup axes this card enumerates when live (e.g. [msi_status, sidedness, line_of_therapy]). Descriptive only.

rationale.description: One-line attestation of why the biology varies by subgroup (or, for blocked/out_of_scope, what the blocker is).

product.description: When live: the derived per-subgroup product id the panorama reads (e.g. coadread-dge-tumor-vs-normal-sensitivity-by-subgroup-v1). First live (indication × axis); coverage grows one product at a time.

assignments_manifest.description: When live: the subgroup-assignments derived-manifest id that supplied the stratum member sets at emit time (e.g. tcga-subgroup-assignments-coadread-v1).

live_products.description: When live across MULTIPLE (indication x axis) products: the coverage registry. Each entry names a per-indication by-subgroup product, its indication, the axes it carries, and the assignments manifest that supplied its member sets. product/assignments_manifest above name the canonical first example; this is the exhaustive list. Provenance/coverage hint (the reader resolves the product per indication).

measurement.description: OPTIONAL. For expression-family cards only, names the measurement modality this card carries. Distinguishes bulk-population vs single-cell vs protein-imaging vs in-situ spatial evidence so the skill layer can emit per-modality sub-verdicts (a target can be bulk-RNA-high but IHC-restricted, and the framework should surface that pattern, not average it away). spatial_transcriptomics / spatial_protein name in-situ SPATIAL evidence (imaging single-cell transcriptomics e.g. Xenium/CosMx/MERFISH, or region-level protein e.g. GeoMx) that additionally carries tissue-architecture / neighbourhood information. Cards outside the expression family omit this field.

sample_context.description: OPTIONAL (2026-07-21). The BIOLOGICAL SAMPLE the card's evidence comes from, ORTHOGONAL to `measurement` (the measurement layer). measurement says HOW it was measured (bulk_rna / bulk_protein_ms / ...); sample_context says WHAT was measured (cell_line / tumor / normal). Both axes are independent — every combination is real (bulk_rna x cell_line = DepMap expression; bulk_rna x tumor = TCGA DGE; bulk_protein_ms x cell_line = Gygi; bulk_protein_ms x tumor = CPTAC). The per-modality sub-verdict view buckets by (measurement, sample_context) so a cell-line-RNA signal is never conflated with a tumor-RNA signal. Defaults from measurement_type (cell_line_* -> cell_line, tumor_* -> tumor); the validator enforces consistency. Cards without a sample substrate (dependency, mutation, mechanism, tractability) omit this.

modality_relevance.description: OPTIONAL (2026-07-23, P4 modality-vector emission). ROUTING METADATA (per DATA_TO_SKILL_CONTRACT.md): declares WHICH modality-fit gates (axis-2) should PULL this card, so a card's evidence lands in the right modality gate rather than being stranded on the biology axis (axis-1). NOT a modality-specific value and NOT a signal — the per-modality SIGNAL is carried by the interpretation rules' `signals:` map (small_molecule/degrader on the intracellular axis; adc/bite_tce/antibody on the surface axis). A card declaring `modality_relevance: [adc,...]` but with no surface-axis rule is 'declared-relevant-but-mute' — the stranded state P4 exists to prevent. DISAMBIGUATION: distinct from the per-edge `modality_relevance` tuple that appears INSIDE signaling-network-mechanism's upstream_regulators struct records (that is struct-internal, this is the card-level routing key). Mirrors the `modality_relevance` key already used on measurement_types in vocabularies/measurement_types.yaml (e.g. surface_confirmation).

measurement_type.description: DATA_TO_SKILL_CONTRACT.md Rule 1 (2026-07-21) — the card's IDENTITY: the single per-target-entity CLAIM it measures (e.g. crispr_lof_dependency, surface_confirmation, normal_tissue_breadth). Must be a key registered in vocabularies/measurement_types.yaml. A card owns exactly one measurement_type; distinct claims (per the concordance test, Rule 2) are distinct cards. OPTIONAL during migration (existing cards are un-migrated; a validator warns, does not error) — REQUIRED for all NEW cards per the frozen identity rule. The type registry declares the value_vocabulary, providers, evidence tiers, grains, and multi_provider_policy; the card names which type it is a view of.

entity_grains.description: DATA_TO_SKILL_CONTRACT.md Rule 5 (2026-07-21) — the CAPABILITY CEILING: the entity grains this card's substrate can emit (a per-sample reader can support target_subtype; an aggregate reader cannot). The runtime query SELECTS a grain within this ceiling; a request above the ceiling gets an honest data_unavailable for that grain and MUST NOT silently fall back to a coarser grain. Values are governed by the grain vocabulary (target | target_indication | target_subtype | target_lineage | cohort | single_cell — extensible by vocabulary entry, never a schema change). OPTIONAL during migration; when present, must be non-empty. Complements the existing `tier` field (channel-precedence tier) — grain is the slicing dimension, tier is the precedence class.

schema_version.description: Version of card.schema.json this spec validates against. Currently always 1; bumps when card.schema.json itself takes a breaking change.

capsule.description: Evidence-capsule projection contract (consumed by _skills_common/evidence_capsule.emit_capsules). OPTIONAL strangler: when present it OVERRIDES the capsule's field-selection heuristics for this card; when absent the emitter falls back to the hint heuristics. `primary_class` names the verdict-driving *_class field (fixes the alphabetical-first mis-pick on multi-class cards); `categorical_fields` names the salient non-numeric summary fields (stage labels, class enums, bool flags, short lists) a numeric-only selector would drop. VERDICT-INERT projection.

primary_class.description: The verdict-driving categorical summary field for this card (e.g. structural_ligandability_class), used as the capsule `class` instead of the alphabetical-first *_class heuristic.

categorical_fields.description: Salient non-numeric summary fields to surface as categorical_anchors in the capsule DATA layer, in priority order.
